meta.hypothesis: After E17 relocated the chem6 1us gap to reaction/diffusion physics, verify whether the IRT rate constants + diffusion coefficients match Geant4 option1 source. If yes, the gap is spatial (radical distribution), not a chemistry-rate bug.
meta.method: Direct line-by-line compare of public/irt-worker.js RXN_TABLE + IRT_D against G4EmDNAChemistry_option1.cc (Geant4 11.4.1) ConstructReactionTable + SetDiffusionCoefficient.

summary.headline: All 9 IRT rate constants + the diffusion coefficients are BIT-IDENTICAL to Geant4 option1 source. The IRT chemistry is a faithful port; the 1us chem6 gap is NOT a rate/diffusion bug.
summary.conclusion: The residual 1us chem6 gap is therefore in the radical SPATIAL DISTRIBUTION, which comes from our deliberately-divergent track-structure physics (Emfietzoglou excitation, SIGMA_EXC_SCALE, fp32 atomics — catalogued in GEANT4_DIVERGENCES.md), not from the chemistry. Combined with E17 (cross-primary is a coupled tradeoff, not the cause), the chem6 gap is now understood: the chemistry is bit-faithful; the gap is inherited from the upstream physics divergences. This is an honest bound, not an open chemistry bug.
